summary: In this excerpt from Book 1 (part 62), the narrator Marcus, also known by the handle M1k3y, is worried that the Xnet he set up now operates on its own and that he and his friends could be jailed for it. He wants to consult Jolu, a friend who works at an ISP called Pigspleen Net. He meets Vanessa (Van) and Jolu at a cafe in the Mission, ostensibly for their Harajuku Fun Madness team meeting, which has become a weekly gathering of grief since the game was canceled and Darryl disappeared. Van, arriving in her school uniform, argues he is putting himself at risk, and the two quarrel over whether resisting the government is worth it.
one_line: Marcus argues with Van at a Mission cafe about his risky Xnet activity, after the game's cancellation and Darryl's disappearance.
key_facts: The narrator says the Xnet, once running, 'had a life of its own' and he could not stop it.
Jolu worked at an Internet Service Provider called Pigspleen Net that had hired him when he was twelve.
The narrator believes Jolu knows more about the net than he does and could help keep them out of jail.
The team meets weekly at their favorite place in the Mission after school, officially for the Harajuku Fun Madness team meeting.
With the game canceled and Darryl gone, the meetings have become a weekly weep-fest supplemented by about six calls and IMs a day.
Vanessa arrived in her girl's school uniform because a school shuttle-bus service forced her to take the long way home, down to the San Mateo bridge and back up into the city.
Vanessa's outfit is described as Sailor Moon style: a pleated skirt, a tunic and knee-socks.
The cafe was full of older emo art students who snickered into their lattes when Vanessa arrived.
Vanessa says the narrator is 'out of your mind' and asks if he is 'actually, totally, really, for-real crazy'.
Vanessa tells the narrator to stop putting himself at risk and says he could go to jail, and not just him, but lots of people.
The narrator's handle M1k3y is now associated with his Xnet use, which frightens him when said aloud in public.
The narrator says he is doing this for Darryl and because the alternative is to let the government get away with it all.
Vanessa says the government is 'They're the government' and doubts they can stop them.
The narrator responds, 'It's still our country... We still have the right to do this.'
